statement: How many digits does the number $5^{40}$ have? You may use the fact that $2^{10} = 1024$.

choices.misconception: I rounded $2^{10}$ to exactly 1000, so I got $5^{40} = 10^{40} \div 10^{12} = 10^{28}$, which has 29 digits, but $2^{40}$ is a bit more than $10^{12}$.
I thought each factor of 5 adds one digit.
I wrote $5^{40} = 25^{20}$ and treated 25 as roughly 10, getting about $10^{20}$, which has 21 digits.
I found that $5^{40}$ is about $9 \times 10^{27}$ and counted only the 27 zeros, forgetting the leading digit.

hints: Multiply $5^{40}$ by $2^{40}$. What do you get?
$5^{40} = \frac{10^{40}}{2^{40}}$. Estimate $2^{40}$ carefully: is it a little more or a little less than $10^{12}$, and which side of a power of 10 does that put the answer?

solutions.reliable: $5^{40} \times 2^{40} = 10^{40}$, so $5^{40} = \frac{10^{40}}{2^{40}}$. Now $2^{40} = 1024^4$, and $1.024^4$ is about $1.1$, so $2^{40} \approx 1.1 \times 10^{12}$. Therefore $5^{40} \approx \frac{10^{28}}{1.1} \approx 9.1 \times 10^{27}$. A whole number between $10^{27}$ and $10^{28}$ has 28 digits. The transferable idea: when an estimate lands next to a power of 10, check which side of it the true value falls on.

whyOnTest: Order-of-magnitude questions test rounding with care, and the trap here is a rounding that lands on the wrong side of a power of 10.
